Formulation
- Brief summary:
  - A 40-year-old patient reports a 2–3 week history of new left-sided facial numbness, reduced hearing on the left, intermittent tinnitus and occasional dizziness. These new somatic neurological/auditory symptoms have precipitated health-related anxiety and episodes of panic (often exacerbated by online searching). Past ENT history includes nasal polyps (intermittent) and a remote episode described as labyrinthitis. The clinician considers Bell's palsy as a possible cause but cannot confirm without face-to-face neurological and ear examination. Factors perpetuating distress include ongoing unexplained symptoms and work impact (reduced training as a jockey). Protective factors include partner support and active engagement with healthcare.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Health-related anxiety/panic related to new neurological/auditory symptoms
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Obtain definitive medical assessment and explanation for symptoms.
  - Reduce panic and anxiety about serious illness.
  - Resume work/training as symptoms allow.
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Provide timely face-to-face medical assessment to evaluate symptoms and reduce health anxiety through clarification and management plan.
  - Assess need for further ENT/neurology investigation and initiate appropriate referrals.
- Actions (Patient):
  - Attend the face-to-face clinic appointment arranged for the same day.
  - Contact the support team number in notes as instructed to confirm/slot the appointment.
  - Report new or worsening symptoms (see clinician instructions) if they occur.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Arrange same-day face-to-face clinic appointment for neurological and ear examination (message to admin to book appointment; clinician has initiated this).
  - Provide support team contact number in patient notes and advise patient to ring to confirm appointment.
  - Perform neurological cranial nerve examination and otoscopic ear inspection at in-person visit; confirm or exclude Bell's palsy and decide on further management/referral (ENT/neurology/imaging) as indicated.
  - Provide reassurance after examination and consider brief strategies for anxiety management or referral to mental health support if anxiety persists after medical clarification.

Secondary Problem: New left-sided facial numbness and reduced hearing (possible Bell's palsy or other neurological/ENT cause)
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Receive diagnostic evaluation and management to address numbness and hearing loss.
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Confirm diagnosis through clinical examination and initiate appropriate treatment or referrals.
- Actions (Patient):
  - Attend the in-person assessment today and describe symptom timeline and any changes.
  - Report any new symptoms immediately (e.g., weakness elsewhere, swallowing/speech/vision changes).
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Conduct targeted neurological and ENT examination; inspect ear and cranial nerve function.
  - If Bell's palsy suspected, initiate appropriate management per local protocols (documentation of planned management not recorded in transcript).
  - If findings suggest alternative pathology or red flags, arrange urgent ENT/neurology referral or imaging as indicated.
